plants.name: Dionaea 'Akai Ryu'
plants.tip: The burgundy only develops in hours of direct sun. In shade it greens up and stays that way until the next season.
plants.colour: Deep burgundy throughout, petioles and traps

plants.name: Dionaea 'Alien'
plants.tip: Distorted traps catch less, so it grows slowly. Leave the traps alone and let it feed itself outdoors in summer.
plants.colour: Green traps with a red interior and blunt, irregular teeth

plants.name: Dionaea 'B52'
plants.tip: Traps this size need a full season of direct sun to build. Rainwater only, as tap water kills it within months.
plants.colour: Green outside, deep red inside, on very large traps

plants.name: Dionaea 'Bohemian Garnet'
plants.tip: Compact and slow. Give it a cold winter rest of three months or it exhausts itself and dies in its second year.
plants.colour: Dark garnet-red rosette, low and compact

plants.name: Dionaea 'Clayton's Red Sunset'
plants.tip: Red interiors fade fast in indirect light. A south-facing spot outdoors from spring onwards keeps the colour.
plants.colour: Bright red trap interiors on green petioles

plants.name: Dionaea 'Coquillage'
plants.tip: The cupped traps rarely close on prey. Feed it nothing; it lives perfectly well on photosynthesis alone.
plants.colour: Green shell-shaped traps, flushed red inside

plants.name: Dionaea 'Cupped Trap'
plants.tip: Fused lobes mean the traps barely function, so never fertilise the soil to compensate. It burns the roots.
plants.colour: Pale green fused cup-shaped traps

plants.name: Dionaea 'Dentate Traps'
plants.tip: Short teeth interlock cleanly and catch well. Keep the pot standing in two centimetres of rainwater.
plants.colour: Green with a red interior and short triangular teeth

plants.name: Dionaea 'Fondue'
plants.tip: Traps distort most in summer heat and look more ordinary in spring. Nothing is wrong with the plant.
plants.colour: Green traps that look melted and run together

plants.name: Dionaea 'Fused Tooth'
plants.tip: The fused teeth leave gaps, so prey escapes. That is fine, as a flytrap needs no insects to survive indoors.
plants.colour: Green with red interiors, teeth fused in pairs

plants.name: Dionaea 'Green Dragon'
plants.tip: The red lining needs direct sun to deepen. Peat and sharp sand only, never potting compost.
plants.colour: Green outside with a deep red trap lining

plants.name: Dionaea 'Holland Red'
plants.tip: Sold everywhere and often potted in the wrong soil. Repot into peat and sand within the first year.
plants.colour: Green petioles with strongly red trap interiors

plants.name: Dionaea 'Jaws'
plants.tip: Vigorous enough to clump quickly. Divide in early spring, before the traps of the new season open.
plants.colour: Green with red interiors and long shark-like teeth

plants.name: Dionaea 'Justina Davis'
plants.tip: Stays green no matter how much sun it gets, so pale colour is not a sign that the light is short.
plants.colour: Entirely green, with no red anywhere even in full sun

plants.name: Dionaea 'Korean Melody Shark'
plants.tip: The traps often fail to shut fully. Leave them be and water from below with rainwater.
plants.colour: Light tangerine traps on vine-like green petioles

plants.name: Dionaea 'Korrigans'
plants.tip: Small and slow to bulk up. Three cold months over winter, then it starts again from the rhizome.
plants.colour: Green cupped traps with short teeth

plants.name: Dionaea 'Louchapates'
plants.tip: The wide flat spines let small prey walk back out. Never make up for it with fertiliser in the soil.
plants.colour: Burgundy traps with long, wide, flattened spines

plants.name: Dionaea 'Microdent'
plants.tip: Short teeth close tightly on gnats. Keep the soil wet at all times; it will not recover from drying out.
plants.colour: Green with red interiors and very short teeth

plants.name: Dionaea 'Mirror'
plants.tip: A mutant with unreliable traps and slow growth. Judge it on the rosette, not on what it catches.
plants.colour: Green traps with fused, mirrored teeth

plants.name: Dionaea 'Petite Dragon'
plants.tip: Small enough to lose in a big pot. Grow it in a shallow container of peat and sand, in full sun.
plants.colour: Small red traps on short green petioles

plants.name: Dionaea 'Red Burgundy'
plants.tip: Colour builds through the season and is deepest by late summer. It will not go red on a shaded sill.
plants.colour: Burgundy-red traps deepening through the season

plants.name: Dionaea 'Red Piranha'
plants.tip: Thick short teeth hold larger prey. Cut off the flower stalk unless you want seed, as flowering sets it back.
plants.colour: Red traps with short, thick, blunt teeth

plants.name: Dionaea 'Royal Red'
plants.tip: One of the darkest, but only in unshaded direct sun. Indoor light turns it a dull green within weeks.
plants.colour: Deep red-purple across the whole plant

plants.name: Dionaea 'Sawtooth'
plants.tip: Uneven teeth make the traps look damaged when they are not. Rainwater or distilled water only.
plants.colour: Green with red interiors and uneven, saw-like teeth

plants.name: Dionaea 'Wacky Traps'
plants.tip: Traps twist and often will not shut. Grow it for the shape and let it photosynthesise.
plants.colour: Green, twisted and irregular traps

plants.name: Dionaea 'Big Mouth'
plants.tip: Broad traps colour up strongly outdoors. Put it out after the last frost and leave it out until autumn.
plants.colour: Wide rounded traps with strong red interiors

plants.name: Dionaea 'Low Giant'
plants.tip: Grows flat rather than upright, so it needs light from directly above rather than from a side window.
plants.colour: Large red traps held low and flat

plants.name: Dionaea 'Ginormous'
plants.tip: Big traps need a deep pot, as the roots go down further than the plant suggests. Rainwater only.
plants.colour: Very large candy-red traps on thick petioles

plants.name: Dionaea 'King Henry'
plants.tip: Fast and free-clumping. Split the clump every second spring or the crowns compete and the traps shrink.
plants.colour: Large traps turning scarlet in full sun

plants.name: Dionaea 'Maroon Monster'
plants.tip: The maroon deepens with direct sun and cold nights. It will look ordinary green in a heated room.
plants.colour: Deep maroon traps edged in apple green

plants.name: Dionaea 'Long Red Fingers'
plants.tip: The long crossed spines are the point of it. Keep it wet and unfed and they lengthen through the season.
plants.colour: Red cupped traps with long, crossed spines

plants.name: Dionaea 'Trichterfalle'
plants.tip: The funnel traps cannot close on prey at all. Treat it as a foliage plant and never fertilise it.
plants.colour: Green funnel-shaped traps, fused at the base

plants.name: Dionaea 'Phalanx'
plants.tip: The long spines need a full season to reach their length. Cut off flower stalks to keep the energy in the traps.
plants.colour: Red traps with exceptionally long red spines

plants.name: Dionaea 'Whale'
plants.tip: Low and wide, so give it a broad shallow pot. It sits happily in a tray of rainwater all summer.
plants.colour: Bright yellow-green, low and wavy traps

plants.name: Dionaea 'Triton'
plants.tip: The largest of the cup-trap forms, and still slow. Do not repot more than once every two years.
plants.colour: Bright yellow-green hooded cup traps

plants.name: Dionaea 'Angel Wings'
plants.tip: Splayed traps still catch well, so it needs no help. Water from the tray and never from above.
plants.colour: Traps splayed wide open, green through yellow to red

plants.name: Dionaea 'Cross Teeth'
plants.tip: Colour swings from green to orange to purple with the light it gets. All of them are healthy.
plants.colour: Cupped traps in green, orange or purple with crossed spines

plants.name: Dionaea 'Spider'
plants.tip: Upright petioles reach for light and will lean badly on a windowsill. Turn the pot weekly.
plants.colour: Green traps on thin, upright petioles

plants.name: Dionaea 'Bristle Tooth'
plants.tip: Vigorous, with red interiors that need direct sun. Give it three cold months of dormancy each winter.
plants.colour: Bright red trap interiors with jagged, irregular teeth

plants.name: Dionaea 'Dracula'
plants.tip: Arched traps and red teeth both fade indoors. It wants outdoor sun from spring to the first frost.
plants.colour: Arched traps banded red outside, with red fang-like teeth
